findings.claim: Since the 2022 vintage Pinot Noir may also be bottled as a red at Hengst, Kirchberg de Barr and Vorbourg.
findings.because: Only Hengst and Kirchberg de Barr were admitted for Pinot Noir from the 2022 vintage (Journal Officiel, 13 May 2022). Vorbourg was added later, by the arrêté of 4 July 2024 amending the Alsace Grand Cru cahier des charges (published 7 July 2024), and applies from the 2024 vintage.
findings.fix: Pinot Noir may also be bottled as a red at Hengst and Kirchberg de Barr since the 2022 vintage, and at Vorbourg since the 2024 vintage.
findings.verifyReason: The explanation is wrong. It says that since the 2022 vintage Pinot Noir may be bottled as a red Grand Cru at Hengst, Kirchberg de Barr and Vorbourg. Only Hengst and Kirchberg de Barr were admitted in 2022. Vorbourg came later, by the arrêté of 4 July 2024 amending the Alsace Grand Cru cahier des charges, published in the Journal Officiel on 7 July 2024. I checked that decree on Légifrance: it opens Vorbourg to red wine for the first time (Pinot Noir, at least 5,500 vines per hectare, at least 11 months of ageing) and describes the red production as recognised in 2024. France 3 Grand Est confirms that Vorbourg may use the Grand Cru name for Pinot Noir from the 2024 harvest, and names Hengst and Kirchberg as the two sites approved in 2022. The question's key is not affected (answer 3: Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris, Muscat). Only the last sentence of the explanation is wrong, and the examiner's fix corrects it.
findings.finalFix: Pinot Noir may also be bottled as a red at Hengst and Kirchberg de Barr since the 2022 vintage, and at Vorbourg since the 2024 vintage.

question.q: Four varieties alone may normally be bottled at Grand Cru level. Which set?
opts: Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris, Auxerrois and Sylvaner
Riesling, Sylvaner, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Noir
Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Blanc and Chardonnay
Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat
question.exp: These are the four noble grapes, and outside a handful of named exceptions the restriction is absolute. Where a single variety is used it is named on the label beside the site, though the sites cleared for a blend name no grape at all. Since the 2022 vintage Pinot Noir may also be bottled as a red at Hengst, Kirchberg de Barr and Vorbourg.

findings.claim: Rangen is the only Grand Cru on volcanic soil
findings.because: The CIVA's own Grand Cru Kitterlé page (Guebwiller) describes a sandstone and volcanic terroir: at its western end the soil is volcanic-sedimentary Carboniferous grauwacke, the same kind of rock as Rangen's. The key (Rangen, the steepest and southernmost) still stands, but the word 'only' is false.
findings.fix: Rangen is the best known of the Grands Crus on volcanic rock, and its slope is severe enough that growers carry washed-out soil back up the hill after storms. The wines are smoky and austere in youth.
findings.verifyReason: The key (Rangen, above Thann) is correct. The explanation's claim that Rangen is "the only Grand Cru on volcanic soil" is false. The CIVA (vinsalsace.com) page for Kitterlé calls its soil "gréso-volcanique" and says that at its western edge "le terroir gréso-volcanique appartient aux grauwackes du carbonifère". That is the same Carboniferous volcanic-sedimentary grauwacke the CIVA Rangen page describes ("roches volcaniques et de sédiments ... grauwackes, de tufs volcaniques ... andésite"). The Rangen page makes no "only volcanic" claim. Its "le seul" line is about something else: Rangen is the only one entirely classified as Grand Cru. Kitterlé is also one of the four options, so a candidate who learns "only volcanic" would carry a false fact about a named distractor. The examiner's fix removes "only" and keeps everything that is correct.
findings.finalFix: Rangen is the best known of the Grands Crus on volcanic rock, and its slope is severe enough that growers carry washed-out soil back up the hill after storms. The wines are smoky and austere in youth.

question.q: The steepest of the Grands Crus, and the southernmost, rises above Thann on dark volcanic rock. Which is it?
question.exp: Rangen is the only Grand Cru on volcanic soil, and its slope is severe enough that growers carry washed-out soil back up the hill after storms. The wines are smoky and austere in youth.
